title: streaming retry & idempotency overhaul: consistent retry-after, resume tokens, and error mapping
author: Evelyn Zhang
description: Motivation: clients integrating with the OpenAI-compatible shim have inconsistent behavior when faced with rate limits and transient overload during streaming responses. Reconnects often produce duplicate outputs or fail to resume, and clients don't have clear guidance whether to back off or reconnect. This PR makes three coordinated changes across the shim, stream proxy, and docs: 1) Normalize Retry-After handling and response codes: 429 remains primary for per-client rate limits; 503 is used to indicate transient server-side backpressure when the request reached the runtime but can't be scheduled. Both endpoints include Retry-After (seconds or HTTP-date) and a structured JSON error with a stable error_code (RWD_RATE_LIMIT | RWD_OVERLOAD). 2) Streaming resume / idempotency: introduce an optional X-Redwood-Resume-Token header emitted on partial/early termination and a guarantee that idempotency-key semantics persist across reconnects. Clients can reconnect with the same Idempotency-Key and Resume-Token to continue a stream without double-application of side effects (function/tool calls) and without re-executing completed steps. 3) Error mapping & compatibility: map legacy OpenAI error strings to consistent Redwood error codes and include an explanation mapping in the docs. The description below lists behavioral guarantees, developer migration notes, and test coverage summary.
commits: Refactor retry header parsing and unify Retry-After semantics (a8c4f2a)
Add resume token emission and validation in stream proxy (d3b9e1c)
Persist idempotency keys across reconnects and add resume token -> offset mapping (e6f7b91)
Map OpenAI error payloads to Redwood canonical error codes (7b2ffd4)
Add integration tests for streaming reconnect and backpressure (4c1d2ab)
changes: src/shim/openai/errors.go: add canonical codes RWD_RATE_LIMIT, RWD_OVERLOAD, RWD_CLIENT_ERROR and map legacy OpenAI error 'rate_limit'/'insufficient_quota' -> RWD_RATE_LIMIT

src/shim/openai/stream_proxy.go: emit X-Redwood-Resume-Token when returning partial chunk with non-terminal status; accept Resume-Token+Idempotency-Key on reconnect and validate offset (new token format v1).
pkg/middleware/retry_after_parser.py: parse both integer-seconds and HTTP-date formats; clamp long Retry-After values to a server-configurable max_backoff to avoid DOS vectors.

pkg/middleware/idempotency_store.go: store resume offsets with idempotency-key namespace; on reconnect ensure previously completed tool-calls are not re-run, respond with 409+RWD_CONFLICT if client attempts conflicting replay.

src/runtime/scheduler/backpressure.go: expose explicit 503 path for runtime overload (RequestAcceptedButDelayed) that bubbles Retry-After and a short backoff suggestion; emit metrics runtime.backpressure.count and runtime.backpressure.avg_wait_ms.

docs/openai_compat/retry_idempotency.md: migration notes for clients, examples for reconnect flow in JS/Python, and recommended best practices for exponential backoff + jitter when Retry-After absent.
tests/integration/stream_resume.test.ts: simulate mid-stream 503 with Retry-After header and verify client can reconnect and resume tokens drive deterministic continuation.
examples/streams/resume-client.js: example reconnect logic that attaches Idempotency-Key and Resume-Token, validates server-supplied resume ranges, and sanity-checks final message deduplication.
tests/unit/retry_after_parsing_test.py: cover edge cases (HTTP-date in different timezones, negative values, very long durations).

release_notes: Improved streaming stability and error semantics: clients should see consistent Retry-After behavior for rate limits and runtime backpressure, be able to resume interrupted streams using server-issued resume tokens, and rely on canonical Redwood error codes for programmatic handling. See docs/openai_compat/retry_idempotency.md for migration steps and examples.
notes_for_ops: Ops: deploy runtime/scheduler change before or at same time as shim; enable new metric runtime.stream.reconnects and set alert threshold > 5 per minute for initial ramp. Rolling deploy recommended. Monitor tests in benchmark-lab/stream-reconnect for regressions.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for Retry-After parsing, idempotency token validation, and integration tests that run simulated reconnect scenarios (including function/tool-call deduplication). CI was flaky on initial run due to a timing-dependent test which was hardened and retried. Local load tests show ~1.2x increase in short-tail p95 while reducing duplicate tool calls to 0% in reconnect scenarios.
migration_guide: Clients: 1) When reconnecting, continue to supply the same Idempotency-Key header; if server returned X-Redwood-Resume-Token include it in Reconnect-Resume-Token header. 2) For backoff, prefer server Retry-After when present; otherwise use exponential backoff with jitter. 3) Update error handling to inspect error.code (RWD_RATE_LIMIT, RWD_OVERLOAD, RWD_CLIENT_ERROR) rather than string matching.
performance_impact: Minor: small increase in p95 under steady load due to extra token validation (~5-10ms per connection) but reduces wasted work under overload by avoiding re-execution of side-effectful steps.
attack_surface_considerations: We clamp Retry-After and require server-signed opaque resume tokens to mitigate replay and enumeration attacks. Resume tokens are HMAC-signed and short-lived (configurable TTL). Token contents are not accepted from clients (they must be returned verbatim).
